problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=⟨2,0,-1⟩+t⟨-2,-7,5⟩+s⟨2,12,5⟩,\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Parametric Equations of a Plane

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector To a Plane Given by Parametric Equation
examples.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane 

$$
\mathbf{r}= \langle -6,3, 2 \rangle + t \langle 4, 2, -1 \rangle + s \langle 4, -3, 2 \rangle,\qquad t,\,s \in (-\infty,\infty).
$$
examples.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $\mathbf{v} = \langle 4, 2, -1 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{w} = \langle 4, -3, 2 \rangle$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{w}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =i-12j-20k \\  & =⟨1,-12,-20⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $\mathbf{n}=\langle 1, -12, -20 \rangle.$

feedback.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $T(7,0,-3)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $T$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}].$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}],\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
